label: late copy-phase steps, gated by input-token identity (g/n/q/l/y/x/h/a/m/u)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L), never on original tokens, the <DEL> step, or the first copy output (recall_idx 0); it requires in_first == 0 (the input is a repeated, fed-back token). It is concentrated on the last 2-3 copy steps (to_go <= 1 holds 76% of mass) and is much stronger for short sequences (L = 3: 33% of copy steps active, L = 4: 12%; top activations are all L = 3 at the second copy step, e.g. 3 q j <DEL> 3 [q]). Within the copy phase it depends on the fed-back input token: g, n, q, l (rate 15-18%) then y, x, h, a, m, u, against ~5% for others. Neither cue alone is enough: position-only gives F1 0.33, token-only 0.35, and the conjunction 0.42 on dev (adding an L <= 4 clause gives 0.44). It is broadly dense across late copy steps, and precision stays low (~0.34).
